sub_palette: classical (latinate) lean + east_asian (japonic) substrate (cross-family fusion, Latinate-leaning)
homeland: Waitalia (the Eagle-Realm of the Rising Sun; Wa- the island-realm + Italia)

blend.lean_parent: classical (latinate: the Roman civic-and-legal spine - the via and iter roads, the castra forts and the urbs cities, the legio and the forum, the gens-line and the lex law-stele, the -us/-um/-a endings and penultimate stress, the imperator-style imperial title, the engineering and law register of a road-and-eagle state)
blend.substrate_parent: east_asian (japonic: the open CV-mora island and shrine words - the shima-isles and the jinja-shrines, the kami of mountain and sea, the rice-and-silk-and-jade staple words, the torii-grove and the castle-town, the daimyo island-house lord)
blend.lean: Latinate-heavy - the legion and the samurai, the forum and the shrine, the eagle over the rising sun: a Roman-Japonic realm grown into one tongue and one rite, where the Roman civic-legal-rule register is the backbone and the Japonic island/shrine/material/staple words are the substrate. Not a ruling elite over a populace - one merged people, one fused language (per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): the forum keeps the law and the shrine keeps the land.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_06 (Roman/Agrippan, Latinate) x BASE_08 (Japonic/Yamataian). FUSION-FIRST (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): a SINGLE fused tongue, one word per concept, derived by principled sound-change from both parents - NOT a slash-pair dual-register gloss. CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Roman (Classical) base = Civilized, Japonic base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Waitalia is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Roman-Japonic realm - the legion and the samurai, the forum and the shrine, the eagle over the rising sun (a Roman west wedded to an island-arc of daimyo houses and kami-shrines). Lean = Latinate (the rule/kin/law/land/civic register, the via/castra/urbs/forum civic spine, the -us/-um/-a endings, penultimate stress, the imperial Imperator title, SOV recut from the substrate); substrate = Japonic (island, shrine, mountain, sea, rice, silk, jade - the land, material and staple words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Latin register (allowed, catalog 5.3), with the Japonic substrate words fused into Latin phonology; DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Latinate canon-morphs PRIMARY (the agrippan column: Tulrius, Orlandus, Gaiandus, Numeno, Realta, Aeternus), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (the yamataian / family_east_asian.json japonic column: Terashi-no-kami, Hagane-no-kami, Iwane-no-kami, recut to Latin shape), never real Roman gods or Shinto kami. All three alignments (per 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are ENGLISH except the empire which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Imperator' (the Roman imperial style) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord, the apt Japonic-substrate co-rank); conlang titles in ruler_native/domain_native (Latin) for NPC dialogue. CSV phonetic profile 'Mora-timed rhythm with balanced rhythm'; grammar 'SOV, Case-inflected agglutinative particles'.

phonology.palette: Classical (Latinate) lean - a e i o u; p t c(=k) b d g f s v l r m n; the endings -us/-a/-um/-ius/-or; penultimate stress; the moderate onset clusters st-/tr-/pr-/cl-/sp- and the geminates ll/ss/tt - taking up an East-Asian (Japonic) substrate: open CV moras, the five vowels a i u e o, the island/shrine/mountain/sea/rice/silk/jade word-stock, rendaku voicing, the -no linking particle. Per the CSV: a mora-timed rhythm carried under a balanced Latin rhythm (the Japonic CV evenness audible beneath the Latin penultimate stress and the -us/-um closes); grammar is SOV, case-inflected with agglutinative particles (the Japonic agglutinative SOV substrate recut onto the Latin case-endings, the -no relational particle latinized to a linking -i-/-o-). Theophoric on the Latinate canon-morphs (Tulrius-, Orlandus-) with the Japonic kami-morphs as the shrine register (Teraso-, Hagano-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV / CVC (Latin) over the Japonic CV moras; Japonic CV-mora roots shed their final open vowel into a Latin -us/-um/-a close or take a Latin nominal ending; clusters st-/tr-/pr-/cl-/sp- (Latin) admitted, geminates ll/ss/tt allowed; penultimate stress (the Latin pattern overrides Japonic pitch-accent); Castra-/Via-/-um construct toponyms over -sima/-yama island-and-mountain elements; the -no particle latinized to a linking vowel.

sound_changes: Japonic open CV-moras adapt to Latin shape: the final open vowel sheds or recuts into a Latin -us/-um/-a/-or close, or the stem hardens consonant-final before taking a Latin nominal ending (yama>iamus, shima>sima, mori>morum, umi>umus, kawa>cavus, jinja>iancia)

Japonic plain consonants map onto the Latin inventory: k>c(=k), s retained, t retained, voiced g/b/d retained, ch>c, sh>s before the Latin vowels; rendaku voicing simplifies to the Latin stop (-gawa root surfaces as -cavus)

Japonic pitch-accent is overridden by Latin penultimate stress; word order is SOV recut with case-inflected agglutinative particles; the Japonic -no linking particle is latinized to a linking -i-/-o- (X-no-Y > X-i-Y)

the Latin a/e/i/o/u with penultimate stress dominate; Japonic e/o admitted in stressed substrate roots; retain the Latin -us/-um/-ius/-or endings and the st-/tr-/pr- clusters, and retain the Japonic open-vowel color of substrate stems; Latin geminates ll/ss/tt permitted
very short Japonic roots take a Latin -us/-um/-a ending to reach a CV(C)-us shape (ko>colus, no>novum/campus-substrate, do>dorum, cha>chaia)
fusion_rules.source_tilt: island/shrine/mountain/sea/coast/material/staple words from Japonic roots (the substrate land and its making - shima, yama, umi, jinja, kome, kinu, hisui, uma, cha), then filtered to Latin phonology; rule/kin-line/law/land/civic/quality/abstract/war words from Latin roots (the lean register - via, castra, urbs, forum, lex, gens, magnus, ferrum, legio); every chosen root then run through the one Latin-shaped sound-law (penultimate stress, -us/-um/-a closes) so the split is invisible at the surface - it all sounds like one Latin-shaped tongue

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic island/shrine/material/staple roots + Latin rule/kin/law/land/civic roots, all run through one Latin-shaped sound-law (CV-moras recut into -us/-um/-a closes, penultimate stress, st-/tr-/pr- clusters, latinized -no linking vowel); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One word per concept, NO slashes.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Roman-descended civic stock keep an inherited gens (clan) name as a binomial/trinomial element (X VALERIUS) woven onto the fused frame; the Japonic-substrate folk keep a reduced -i- house-link (latinized from -no-) before the given name; nobility carry the gens and an earned cognomen. The throne fuses both - an Imperator who heads a gens and also an island gens-i- house with a -i- shrine-lineage. Order given-first.
morphology.compounding_rule: Latin construct-chains (Castra-[name], Via-[name], [adjective|resource](stem) + feature-word eliding before a vowel) layered over fused feature-compounds (quality + island/shrine element): the capital Waitalia (the eagle-realm, aquila + wa + -ia), Castra-Ferra (the iron-fort), Atriamus (black-mountain isle, ater + iamus), Insima-Magna (the great isle). Quality + feature in the Latin manner: magnus (great), ater (black), sacer (sacred) lead the compound; rendaku voicing simplifies to the Latin stop.

title_ladder.government: feudal (a fused eagle-and-shrine realm: the Imperator and his patrician kin at the crown over the island-provinces, the Comes-counts over the urbs civic-provinces, the great island-houses - the daimyo of the shrine-isles - sworn beneath; the pontifex-priesthood of the forum and the kannushi-shrine-keepers serve the one rite together, the legion and the samurai under one eagle)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Latin native ladder, ascending, beneath an English display ladder (Baron/Marquis/Count/[Daimyo]/Prince/King/[Imperator]). The empire-tier DISPLAY ruler is the approved commonly-known foreign term 'Imperator' (the Roman imperial style, its native form remaining Imperator) and the duchy-tier DISPLAY ruler is 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord, the Japonic-substrate co-rank, its native Latin form remaining Dux); all other display tiers are English. Native: Castellanus (castle-lord) barony; Limitanus (frontier-warden, from the Roman limes/limitanei) march; Comes (companion-count) county; Dux (war-leader, the duke - styled the Daimyo) duchy over a Ducatus; Princeps (first-citizen prince) principality; Rex (king) kingdom over a Regnum; Imperator (commander, the imperial style) empire over the Imperium. The Japonic substrate keeps its shugo-governor and kannushi-priest beneath the Roman crown; the pontifex of the forum and the kannushi of the torii stand together. Rank native-forms use the real Latin register (allowed); 'Imperator' and 'Daimyo' are the approved foreign display terms.
title_ladder.heir: Caesar (heir-designate to the Imperator; the crown prince)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except the empire which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Imperator' (the Roman imperial style) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord). The *_native conlang (Latin) forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Roman-descended civic stock carry a praenomen (personal) + nomen (gens/clan, inherited) + cognomen (earned, optional); the Japonic-substrate folk add a reduced -i- shrine-lineage (latinized from -no-) before the given name; order given-first (both parents agree - the Roman praenomen-first and the reshaped Japonic clan-link resolve to given-first on the fused frame).
people_name_convention.dual_register: the patrician civic register carries the full tripartite gens (praenomen + nomen + cognomen) on the morphed canon-stems; the island-shrine substrate carries fused given names on the kami-morphs (Teraso-, Hagano-) with -rus/-ca/-marus endings recut to the lean Latin phonology; the throne fuses both - a gens-bearing Imperator who also heads an island house.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Roman devotional praenomina lead, derived from the Latinate canon-morphs: Tulrian, Orlandus, Gaiandus, Numenius, Realtus (m), Realta, Numia (f); the shrine register builds on the Japonic kami-morphs: Teraso- (from Terashi), Hagano- (from Hagane), Iwano- (from Iwane), e.g. Terasomarus, Mery-Meguma latinized to Megumarus; names honoring Teraso-the-Shining.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Latinate canon-morphs PRIMARY (the agrippan column, the canonical pantheon keys: Tulrius, Orlandus, Gaiandus, Numeno, Realta, Aeternus), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (family_east_asian.json theonym_sets.japonic, the yamataian column, recut to Latin shape: Teraso, Hagano, Iwano, Numeno-no-kami, Megumarus, Aeternus-no-kami), never real Roman gods or Shinto kami. The fused rite identifies the temple-power and the shrine-kami as one face - the eagle and the rising sun as one: the pontifex of the forum-temple and the kannushi of the torii keep the same powers. All three alignments; the law-stele and the civic cult fused with the household shrine and the ancestral kami, the legion's oath and the samurai's way under one heaven.
religion.the_one: Aeternus (the One / True God; Jp shrine-name Takamus-no-kami) - the distant Ancient One, the High-Heaven One above the myriad powers, honored in liturgy not petitioned

Tulrius.gloss: the sun and right-rule, the rayed sun-disc and the rising sun

Orlandus.gloss: iron, oath, war, the blade and the eagle

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Aeternus, Tulrius the just sun, Orlandus of the sworn oath, Realta the merciful, Numeno of the law - at the forum-temple and the torii-grove alike, and names the Chaotic powers the brood of the great serpent Lusanto or the aramus (the wild spirits), warded; the law-stele and the civic rite, the legion's oath and the samurai's way, bind together
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the deified dead (the divi of the gens inscribed on the law-stele and the senzavi enshrined at the household iantemplum) and the civic-and-isle spirits of the forum and the shrine-isles; the great powers invoked at temple and torii situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the war-flame and the devouring serpent, the storm-kami and the mountain-oni - and names the Lawful powers, and Aeternus, as the tyrant-powers to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the brood of the great serpent Lusanto (Latin) or the aramus (Japonic wild spirits), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Maraxus the Tyrant-Flame (Jp Takebus the War-Flame); Vacidus -> Vacidus the Unmaker (Jp Utsurus the Devouring Void); Lusanto -> Lusanto the Coin-Serpent (Jp Koganus-Orochus the gold serpent).

clergy_ladder.7: Pontifex (high priest) / Gujus (chief priest, from Japonic guji)
clergy_ladder.9: Pontifex Maximus / Saisus (high priest of the realm, from Japonic saishu)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Collegium (college/order) of the forum-temple or the Iantemplum (shrine-isle temple) of [power]: 'the Collegium of the Dawn Throne (Tulrius)', 'the Iantemplum of Teraso', within its sacred court and torii-grove.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified founders and heroes (Divus/Diva [name], the justified dead) venerated at the civic temples, and the great ancestors enshrined as kami at the isle-iantemplum (the honored dead); 'Divus [name]' and 'the kami [name]'.
